title: Architect an isolated multi-tenant Next.js SaaS
businessContext: A SaaS proposes deriving its tenant from an arbitrary Host header and caching every dashboard by pathname.
problemStatement: Design the system for 2,000 tenants; 10,000 peak reads/second; private account data. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Resolve only admitted domains to tenants.
Enforce tenant membership on every read and mutation.
Keep public assets cacheable without caching private dashboards globally.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 2,000 tenants; 10,000 peak reads/second; private account data
functional: Resolve only admitted domains to tenants.
Enforce tenant membership on every read and mutation.
Keep public assets cacheable without caching private dashboards globally.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Terminate traffic at a trusted ingress and resolve a normalized, allowlisted domain to a server-owned tenant ID.

A custom domain can change ownership while an old cache entry remains. Make domain changes an audited workflow with verification, cache/version rotation and a bounded propagation SLO. Reject ambiguous Host/forwarded-host inputs at the trusted boundary.
alternativeApproaches: Compare isolation needs, regional requirements, noisy-neighbor budgets and operational cost. Shared infrastructure can work with strong logical boundaries; high-risk tenants may justify separate deployments and data partitions. Deployment isolation does not remove application authorization.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Attempt cross-tenant IDs, forged domains and action calls outside Proxy coverage.
Warm caches in tenant A before requesting the same pathname in B.
Revoke membership and verify the documented access-revocation bound.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
